Our aim is to characterize the physical properties and the environment of the submillimeter galaxy AzTEC-3 at $z = 5.3$ and the lensed quasar BRI 0952$-0115$ at $z = 4.4$, and to set a limit on the polarization properties of the two sources.

In this study, we explored the environment, searched for magnetic-field signatures, and examined possible outflow properties of two galaxies in the early Universe: the quasar BRI 0952-0115 (hereafter BRI0952) at $z=4.433$ and the massive submillimeter galaxy (SMG) AzTEC-3 at $z=5.3,$ utilizing high-resolution ALMA band-7 [C ii] observations.

We report serendipitous detections of [C ii] emission from two previously unreported companion sources around BRI0952 and new detections of [C ii] emission from three companions surrounding AzTEC-3. These companions are each located within 3$\,''$ (18 kpc) of the central source.
